> ClunkeyShell is a custom 3D-printed enclosure and sensor-mount system for Clunkey Rover, my four-wheel robotics project inspired by my experience with FIRST Robotics. I want to design a case that organizes and protects the ESP32 controller and electronics, with mounting points for the ultrasonic sensor and room for wiring. I'll model the parts with real dimensions and tolerances so they can fit together when printed. The design will support both phone-controlled driving and autonomous obstacle avoidance.

## Design

### 2026-10-16 – # ClunkeyShell — Week 2 Design Journal

**2.5h**

# ClunkeyShell — Week 2 Design Journal

Today, I worked on my ClunkeyShell project for Hack Club Half Life using Onshape. I imported my concept model and explored its three main parts: the enclosure base, the lid, and the ultrasonic sensor mount. I used the Measure tool to check the enclosure's dimensions. The base measures approximately 100 mm long, 70 mm wide, and 25 mm high. I also captured screenshots of the model and measurements to document my progress.

This session helped me understand how individual CAD parts can come together as one design. I also learned that checking dimensions is important before preparing a model for 3D printing. My next step is to compare these measurements with my actual electronics and rover chassis, then adjust the design if needed. ClunkeyShell is still a concept, so I need to verify that the components fit correctly before considering it ready to print.

### 2026-10-16 – # Week 2: ClunkeyShell Enclosure Design

**2h**

# Week 2: ClunkeyShell Enclosure Design

This week, I worked on the design of ClunkeyShell, an enclosure for my ClunkeyCore rover project. I explored how the ESP32 board, ultrasonic sensor, two motor-driver modules, and battery holder could fit inside the enclosure. I also used Onshape to review the CAD layout and create a preliminary design sketch showing an exploded view of the components and a possible assembled layout.

While planning the design, I realized that the enclosure needs enough space for the electronics, wiring, and connections. I explored a proposed shell size of 150 × 100 × 30 mm, but the dimensions and component clearances still need to be verified. The design is not finished yet, so my next step is to arrange the components more precisely and check that everything fits before preparing the enclosure for 3D printing.

This process helped me think more carefully about space, component placement, and how to turn a concept into a practical engineering design.

### 2026-10-18 – **ClunkeyCore — Circuit Simulation and Design Progress**

**5h**

**ClunkeyCore — Circuit Simulation and Design Progress**

Today, I worked on the ClunkeyCore rover project in BenchTwin. I added the ESP32, TB6612FNG motor driver, ultrasonic distance sensor, resistors, battery holder, and four DC motors. I connected the circuit components individually and addressed the wiring warnings until BenchTwin reported that nothing needed attention.

I also added a simulated 4WD robot chassis plate as the starting point for the rover's base. My next step is to plan the placement of the wheels, motors, battery, and electronics around the chassis. I will continue refining the design tomorrow and check the component clearances before considering the physical layout complete.
